To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HECIL is the first error correction algorithm for long reads that leverages the information from short reads, that HECIL significantly outperforms state of the art error correction algorithms for long reads on diverse real data, and that the iterative learning paradigm of HECIL further improves the performance by incorporating knowledge from previous iterations.

HECIL: (1) is a novel hybrid error correction framework for third-generation sequencing reads that outperforms state of the art methods on diverse real data; (2) is the first method to incorporate an iterative learning paradigm to further improve the correction policy at every iteration; (3) is a scalable method that can correct long reads in a matter of minutes; and (4) is a user-friendly method that can be easily integrated with existing genome assemblers.

HECIL is the first error correction algorithm for long reads with a hybrid correction policy that is learned from short read alignments, and that HECIL with iterative learning is the best performing algorithm for long reads in terms of all evaluation metrics.
